name: Narsingdi
tagline: The textile country northeast of Dhaka — a 2,500-year-old city at Wari-Bateshwar, the country's largest cloth market at Baburhat, and orchards heavy with lotkon.

guide.bestTime: October to February for cool, dry weather; June to August if you want to see the lotkon and banana orchards in fruit.
guide.gettingThere: About 50–60 km northeast of Dhaka on the Dhaka–Sylhet highway and the Dhaka–Chittagong/Sylhet railway. Direct trains stop at Narsingdi station; by road it is roughly 1.5–3 hours depending on traffic.
guide.difficulty: Easy — well connected by road and rail, and comfortably day-trippable from Dhaka.

mustVisit.name: Wari-Bateshwar Ruins
mustVisit.description: The excavated remains of a fortified urban settlement around 2,500 years old — among the oldest known cities in Bangladesh, with paved roads, a fort and ancient coins.
mustVisit.history: Occupied roughly from the 6th century BCE, the site yielded punch-marked coins (first noticed by villagers in 1933 and gathered by teacher Hanif Pathan) and Northern Black Polished Ware. Major excavations by Jahangirnagar University from 2000 revealed the scale of the ancient settlement.
tips: A landmark archaeological site — read up before going
Combine with the Shah Irani shrine in Belabo

mustVisit.name: Baburhat (Shekherchar) Cloth Market
mustVisit.description: Reputedly the largest wholesale cloth market in Bangladesh — thousands of shops and hundreds of trucks dispatched daily, the trading heart of the district's vast weaving industry.
mustVisit.history: Beside the Dhaka–Sylhet highway at Sekherchar, Baburhat anchors a region long called a 'Manchester of the East' for its handloom and powerloom output. It is busiest from Friday to Sunday, when traders come from across the country.
mustVisit.bestTime: Friday–Sunday daytime, when the market is fullest
tips: Go on a trading day to see the bustle at its peak
A window into the country's handloom heartland

mustVisit.name: Shah Irani Mazar
mustVisit.description: The mausoleum of Shah Irani, a 14th-century preacher who settled at Habashpur, in Sultanate-style architecture.
mustVisit.history: Shah Irani is remembered as an Iranian saint who came to the region after the conquest of Sylhet in 1303 and is credited with spreading Islam locally; he died in the 1350s. His shrine at Habashpur in Belabo remains a place of local devotion.
tips: Pair with the Wari-Bateshwar ruins in the same direction
Be respectful — it is an active shrine

mustVisit.name: Bhai Girish Chandra Sen's House & Museum
mustVisit.description: The ancestral home of Girish Chandra Sen, the first translator of the Qur'an into Bengali, now a museum at Panchdona.
mustVisit.history: Girish Chandra Sen (c. 1835–1910), a Brahmo missionary and scholar, completed the first full Bengali translation of the Qur'an in 1886. His house at Panchdona was opened as a museum in 2017.
tips: A quiet literary-heritage stop just north of town
Pair with a stroll through Panchdona

mustVisit.name: Dream Holiday Park
mustVisit.description: A large amusement and water park at Chaitaba near Panchdona, beside the Dhaka–Sylhet highway, with rides, a water park and cottages.
mustVisit.history: Opened in August 2011 on around 37 bighas, Dream Holiday Park has grown into one of the district's most popular family day-trip destinations, drawing visitors from Dhaka and beyond.
mustVisit.bestTime: Daytime; cooler months for the rides
tips: Good for families travelling with children
Right on the highway, easy to reach from Dhaka

mustVisit.name: Lotkon & Banana Orchards of Shibpur
mustVisit.description: The heart of Narsingdi's lotkon belt — orchards of the tangy Burmese grape and sweet sagar bananas around Shibpur, the source of the district's nickname, 'the land of lotkon'.
mustVisit.history: Shibpur, especially around Joynagar, grows the great majority of the district's lotkon, and Narsingdi's bananas have been prized since they reached the tables of the Nawabs of Dhaka. The orchards are at their best in the summer harvest.
mustVisit.bestTime: June–August for the lotkon and banana harvest
tips: Visit in the summer to see the orchards in fruit
Buy lotkon fresh from the growers

specialties.name: Lotkon (Burmese Grape)
specialties.description: Narsingdi's most famous fruit — small, tangy-sweet lotkon grown across Shibpur and Belabo, now exported as well as sold across the country.
specialties.venue: Shibpur and Belabo orchards; summer markets

specialties.name: Handloom Weaving
specialties.description: The district is a national weaving hub — Baburhat is the country's largest cloth wholesale market, with Shibpur and Madhabdi major handloom and powerloom centres.

famousPeople.name: Bhai Girish Chandra Sen
famousPeople.knownFor: Brahmo missionary and scholar who made the first full translation of the Qur'an into Bengali (1886) — born at Panchdona, now in Narsingdi, where his house is a museum.

famousPeople.name: Alauddin Al Azad
famousPeople.knownFor: Major Bengali novelist, poet and critic and an Ekushey Padak winner — born in 1932 at Ramnagar village, Raipura upazila, Narsingdi.

famousPeople.name: Birsrestha Matiur Rahman
famousPeople.knownFor: Fighter pilot and recipient of the Bir Sreshtho, the highest gallantry award of 1971; though born in Old Dhaka, his family home is at Ramnagar in Raipura, Narsingdi.

famousPeople.name: Shamsur Rahman
famousPeople.knownFor: A leading modern Bengali poet; born in Old Dhaka, with his ancestral home at Paratoli near Raipura, Narsingdi.

didYouKnow: Wari-Bateshwar in Belabo is one of Bangladesh's oldest known urban settlements — a fortified city roughly 2,500 years old, with paved roads and punch-marked coins.
Narsingdi's Baburhat is widely regarded as the largest wholesale cloth market in Bangladesh, with thousands of shops and hundreds of trucks leaving daily.
The district is nicknamed 'the land of lotkon' — its tangy Burmese grape is exported to the Middle East and Europe.
Narsingdi's Amrita Sagar bananas were once prized enough to reach the tables of the Nawabs of Dhaka, carried to the city in dedicated railway compartments.
Bhai Girish Chandra Sen, who made the first complete Bengali translation of the Qur'an in 1886, was born at Panchdona in Narsingdi.
